short: The annual GST return that reconciles a year of GST filings.
seoTitle: GSTR-9 — Meaning, Applicability and Due Date
metaDescription: GSTR-9 is the annual GST return that consolidates a financial year of GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B filings into one reconciled statement. Who files it, and when.
definition: GSTR-9 is the annual return under GST that consolidates a full financial year of a taxpayer's monthly and quarterly filings — GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B — into a single reconciled statement of outward supplies, input tax credit and tax paid.
bodyHtml:
Who has to file GSTR-9

Filing is mandatory once aggregate turnover in the financial year crosses ₹2 crore. Below that it is optional. A separate reconciliation statement, GSTR-9C, applies once turnover crosses ₹5 crore and ties the annual return back to the audited financial statements.

Why it is a reconciliation, not a fresh filing

GSTR-9 does not re-declare the year; it reconciles what was already filed. If the monthly returns were clean and input tax credit was matched against GSTR-2B through the year, the annual return is straightforward. If they were not, GSTR-9 is where a year of mismatches surfaces at once — which is why the work belongs in the monthly close, not in December.

The due date

GSTR-9 for a financial year is generally due by 31 December of the following year, unless extended. Thresholds and dates change through notifications, so confirm the current position before filing.

faq.question: Is GSTR-9 mandatory for every GST-registered business?
faq.answer: No. It is mandatory once aggregate turnover crosses ₹2 crore in the financial year. Below that threshold it is optional, though some businesses file it voluntarily for a clean record.

faq.question: What is the difference between GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C?
faq.answer: GSTR-9 is the annual return itself. GSTR-9C is an additional reconciliation statement, required above ₹5 crore turnover, that reconciles the annual return with the audited accounts.
